label: Clickhouse
description: Tools to query and explore a ClickHouse database

tools.name: DiscoverDatabases
tools.description: Discover all the databases in the ClickHouse database.

tools.name: DiscoverSchemas
tools.description:
Discover all the schemas in the ClickHouse database.

Note: ClickHouse doesn't have schemas like PostgreSQL, so this returns a default schema name.

tools.name: DiscoverTables
tools.description:
Discover all the tables in the ClickHouse database when the list of tables is not known.

ALWAYS use this tool before any other tool that requires a table name.

tools.name: ExecuteSelectQuery
tools.description:
You have a connection to a ClickHouse database.
Execute a SELECT query and return the results against the ClickHouse database.
No other queries (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, etc.) are allowed.

ONLY use this tool if you have already loaded the schema of the tables you need to query.

The final query will be constructed as follows:
SELECT {select_query_part} FROM {from_clause} JOIN {join_clause}
WHERE {where_clause} HAVING {having_clause}
ORDER BY {order_by_clause} LIMIT {limit} OFFSET {offset}

When running queries, follow these rules which will help avoid errors:
* Never "select *" from a table. Always select the columns you need.
* Always order your results. Use the most important columns or the primary key if you're unsure.
* Always use case-insensitive queries to match strings in the query.
* Always trim strings in the query.
* Prefer LIKE queries over direct string matches or regex queries.
* Only join on columns that are indexed or the primary key. Do not join on arbitrary columns.
* ClickHouse is case-sensitive, so be careful with table and column names.

parameters.name: select_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the SELECT keyword with a comma separated list of columns you wish to return. Do not include the SELECT keyword.

parameters.name: from_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the FROM keyword. Do not include the FROM keyword.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return. This is the LIMIT clause of the query. Default: 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of rows to skip.  This is the OFFSET clause of the query.  Default: 0.

parameters.name: join_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the JOIN keyword. Do not include the JOIN keyword. If no join is needed, leave this blank.

parameters.name: where_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the WHERE keyword. Do not include the WHERE keyword. If no where clause is needed, leave this blank.

parameters.name: having_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the HAVING keyword. Do not include the HAVING keyword. If no having clause is needed, leave this blank.

parameters.name: group_by_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the GROUP BY keyword. Do not include the GROUP BY keyword. If no group by clause is needed, leave this blank.

parameters.name: order_by_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the ORDER BY keyword. Do not include the ORDER BY keyword. If no order by clause is needed, leave this blank.

parameters.name: with_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the WITH keyword when basing the query on a virtual table. If no WITH clause is needed, leave this blank.

tools.name: GetTableSchema
tools.description:
Get the schema/structure of a ClickHouse table in the ClickHouse database
when the schema is not known, and the name of the table is provided.

This tool should ALWAYS be used before executing any query.
All tables in the query must be discovered first,
so that their exact names are known.

parameters.name: schema_name
parameters.description: The schema to get the table schema of

parameters.name: table_name
parameters.description: The table to get the schema of

summary:
## ClickHouse Toolkit

Arcade toolkit for connecting to and querying a ClickHouse database — enabling schema discovery, table exploration, and read-only SQL execution.

## Capabilities

- **Database & schema discovery**: Enumerate all databases and retrieve schema information (returns a default schema name, since ClickHouse does not use PostgreSQL-style schemas).
- **Table discovery**: List all tables in the database; intended to be run before any query so exact table names are known.
- **Schema inspection**: Fetch the full structure of a specific table, including column names and types, before constructing queries.
- **Read-only query execution**: Run `SELECT` statements with full support for joins, filtering, ordering, pagination (`LIMIT`/`OFFSET`), and aggregation (`HAVING`); no write operations (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`) are permitted.

## Secrets

`CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING` — A connection string that encodes all credentials and connection parameters needed to reach your ClickHouse instance. ClickHouse supports multiple connection string formats depending on the client driver; a typical format is `clickhouse://[user]:[password]@[host]:[port]/[database]` or the HTTP-equivalent `http://[user]:[password]@[host]:[port]/[database]`. Obtain the host, port, default database, and credentials from your ClickHouse deployment — for ClickHouse Cloud, find these on the **Connect** page of your service in the [ClickHouse Cloud console](https://clickhouse.cloud); for self-hosted instances, consult your administrator or your server's `config.xml` / `users.xml`. Ensure the user has at minimum `SELECT` privileges on the target database and tables.

For configuring secrets in Arcade, see [Tool Secrets](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets). You can also manage secrets directly at https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets.
